item.text:
**8B.6 Research Note: Andrés Manuel López Obrador (2024)**

Bottom line: the 2024 record is mixed. AMLO did convert several declared goals into visible state action and delivery machinery, especially in education, health, welfare transfers, tax enforcement, disaster response, and succession. But he also used state power in ways that undercut neutral oversight and independent scrutiny, which weakens the “implementation rather than slogans” case.

- **La Escuela es Nuestra ha beneficiado al 99% de los planteles del país** | Programas para el Bienestar | 2024-06-26 | https://programasparaelbienestar.gob.mx/la-escuela-es-nuestra-ha-beneficiado-al-99-de-los-planteles-del-pais/  
  Claim: The government says the school program reached 173,651 schools, covered 99% of basic-education campuses, and delivered direct funds through parent committees for concrete school improvements.  
  IDs: 8B.6, 6A, 6C

- **Banco del Bienestar distribuye 26.5 millones de tarjetas para pago de pensiones, becas y apoyos del Gobierno de la 4T** | Presidencia de México | 2024-07-05 | https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/banco-del-bienestar-distribuye-26-5-millones-de-tarjetas-para-pago-de-pensiones-becas-y-apoyos-del-gobierno-de-la-4t/  
  Claim: AMLO’s government had a large, concrete payment infrastructure in place for pensions, scholarships, and benefits, showing that the welfare agenda was operationalized through direct delivery rather than speeches only.  
  IDs: 8B.6, 6A, 6C, 8A.2

- **Avanza consolidación de IMSS Bienestar con esfuerzos de gobiernos federal y de 23 estados** | IMSS | 2024-01-19 | https://www.imss.gob.mx/prensa/archivo/202401/026  
  Claim: The health rollout was described as being in active implementation across 23 states, with funding, hospital and clinic coverage, basification of staff, specialist hiring, and large increases in consultations and surgeries.  
  IDs: 8B.6, 6A, 6C, 8A.2

- **Mexico's next president will have to boost tax take to pay for social programs** | Reuters | 2024-06-03 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/mexicos-next-president-will-have-to-boost-tax-take-to-pay-for-social-programs-3467628  
  Claim: Reuters said AMLO loosened spending in his final year to finish flagship infrastructure and support a surge in welfare programs, showing real budgetary translation of declared priorities, even if it widened the deficit.  
  IDs: 8B.6, 6A, 6C, 8A.2

- **Gobierno federal presenta caso de evasión fiscal de Totalplay; debe más de mil 500 millones de pesos al SAT** | Presidencia de México | 2024-03-15 | https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/gobierno-federal-presenta-caso-de-evasion-fiscal-de-totalplay-debe-mas-de-mil-500-millones-de-pesos-al-sat/  
  Claim: The administration publicly pursued a tax-evasion case against a politically connected company, which is evidence of enforcement capacity and anti-privilege implementation rather than purely symbolic anti-corruption messaging.  
  IDs: 8B.6, 8A.2, 7A.1

- **AMLO reconoce represión violenta en homicidio de normalista de Ayotzinapa** | El Economista | 2024-07-16 | https://www.eleconomista.com.mx/amlo_reconoce_abuso_de_autoridad_en_homicidio_de_normalista_de_ayotzinapa-vf20240311mp4.html  
  Claim: AMLO acknowledged police violence in Veracruz, said officers “should not have acted that way,” and said two officers were detained, which is concrete state response rather than empty rhetoric.  
  IDs: 8B.6, 8A.2, 7B.1

- **Mexico's sweeping judicial overhaul formally takes effect** | Reuters | 2024-09-15 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/mexicos-sweeping-judicial-overhaul-formally-takes-effect-3616588  
  Claim: Reuters reported the reform was one of AMLO’s major end-of-term victories, but critics said it weakened judicial independence and investor confidence. This shows implementation, but also that the implementation was institutionally corrosive rather than simply effective state reach.  
  IDs: 8B.6, 8A.4, 8A.5, 7A.2

- **Mexico: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report** | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/mexico/freedom-net/2024  
  Claim: Freedom House said a covert SEDENA cyberspace unit monitored critics and used inauthentic accounts, and that the government used insecurity to justify expanded surveillance with little accountability. That is observable state reach, but in a surveillance/propaganda direction that cuts against clean, legitimate implementation.  
  IDs: 8B.6, 8A.3, 8A.5, 7B.2

- **Mexico: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report** | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/mexico/freedom-world/2024  
  Claim: Freedom House said the federal protection mechanism had protected hundreds of journalists and activists, but was underfunded and not always effective; it also noted persistent attacks on the press and dependence on government advertising. This is mixed evidence: some real state capacity, but incomplete and politically constrained.  
  IDs: 8B.6, 7B.1, 8A.5

- **México** | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/mexico  
  Claim: The Reuters Institute described AMLO’s final year as full of verbal attacks on journalists and highlighted the NYT phone-number episode. That is negative evidence that rhetoric sometimes substituted for, or actively undermined, responsible governance.  
  IDs: 8B.6, 7B.1, 8A.3

- **If you want the shortest calibration read:** AMLO in 2024 was not “speeches only.” He converted several priorities into real institutions, transfers, and enforcement. But the same year also showed that he used state machinery to weaken independent checks and intimidate critics, so the implementation was substantial but not cleanly legitimacy-building.
